identity.title: CLEAR: Context-Aware Learning with End-to-End Mask-Free Inference for Adaptive Video Subtitle Removal

problem.claim: Video subtitle removal for localization and media re-editing.

gap.claim: Existing mask-guided diffusion methods are described as annotation- and fine-tuning-intensive, dependent on explicit mask sequences at inference, and unable to adapt static priors to quality variations.

contributions.claim: A self-supervised prior-learning stage uses pixel differences from video pairs as weak supervision to learn subtitle features without annotations.
A LoRA-based adaptive-refinement stage preserves pretrained visual priors while enabling parameter-efficient, mask-free end-to-end inference without external detection modules.
Adaptive focal weighting adjusts prior influence using local quality assessment to address varied subtitle styles and noisy guidance signals.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize CLEAR as establishing a new paradigm for efficient video text removal without inference-time mask dependencies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior multilingual subtitle-removal performance while using only 0.77% trainable parameters.

narrative_sequence.summary: Subtitle removal is framed as important, while existing mask-guided diffusion approaches are described as inefficient, inference-complex, and insufficiently adaptive.
CLEAR is introduced as a lightweight adapter-based framework with three technical innovations.
Stage I learns occlusion guidance from pixel differences; Stage II uses LoRA for parameter-efficient mask-free inference; adaptive focal weighting modulates prior influence by local quality.
The authors report superior multilingual performance with 0.77% trainable parameters and no inference-time mask dependency.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs each identified limitation with a named mechanism: weak supervision for annotation dependence, LoRA for training and inference efficiency, and quality-conditioned weighting for variable guidance.

lessons.interpretation: This creates a traceable problem-to-design rationale that helps readers assess why each component is included.
lessons.application: When presenting a multi-component method, map every component explicitly to a stated bottleneck and retain the operational condition it addresses.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when components are exploratory or their intended bottleneck cannot be stated without speculative attribution.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide datasets, baselines, evaluation metrics, or numerical performance comparisons supporting the claim of superior performance.
It does not report ablations, computational cost beyond the 0.77% trainable-parameter figure, or the conditions under which adaptive weighting improves results.
